❓ **Q1** — When an upstream's licence no longer matches its notice at re-pull, should `check-vendored-skills.js --upstream` only warn, or block? The question is also posted on #1951 (the licence-drift ticket).

Checked: nothing reads `--upstream`'s exit code. Its only caller is a by-hand runbook, `docs/research/glossary-rename.md:250`, which an agent reads, and `scripts/lib/check.js:170` exits 0 on a warning. Both notice sections carry "Copyright (c) 2026" (commit `534b71b6c`), so a harmless year bump in 2027 is plausible.
Unmeasured: how often the two upstreams edit their LICENSE files. The sandbox's `gh` stub reaches no repo. I couldn't search for past rulings either, because the stub reaches no tracker.

(A) Keep LICENCE-MOVED a warning. The report already says which section to refresh and gives the command to fetch the new text.
Confidence: 60% (50% - 70%). Nothing acts on the exit code, so the person reading the report is the only safeguard either way. Proof that someone had skimmed past a mismatch would move this.
